reviews.comment: Funny guy take it easy now that you are done teaching!

You know those memes about upper level/major-specific professors vs 101 professors? Those very much apply to Maness; always making jokes about being hungover, swears like a sailor, and doesn't trip about late assignments. He is hilarious, relaxed, and knowledgable. Not exactly an easy A, but probably one of the easiest 400 level Econ classes at A&M

Dr. Maness does full time work in the Health Economics field so his class was really interesting. I enjoyed this class a lot more from him than I did in 323. The material is straight forward and fairly easy. There is a decent amount of outside reading so do that in advance and you should be fine. I recommend taking for a laid back econ class!!

Dr. Maness has the ability to truly explain the material in a way that you can understand it. He treats students like adults and doesnt sugar coat things. Class isnt work-heavy, so study for 3 tests or so and youll do just fine. He was ready to answer questions and strives to have his students understand the material. Great professor!
He is a super lazy lecturer, hard grader and does not help you at all. His tests came out of left field and did not really give you anything to study other than his notes.

He is a good professor, and he is willing to help. People who complain there are only three tests and that is your whole grade sorry that is college. Econ 323 is not the class he usually teaches, though. I'd take him for any class!
reviews.ratingTags: Graded by few things--Clear grading criteria--Hilarious

reviews.comment: There are a couple of flaws in his course: To begin, your grade in the class is based on three exams, no homework or quiz cushions either. There is no margin for error in this class. Second, Dr. Maness is a lazy lecturer. He doesnt elaborate enough over the examples he provides in lecture. My advice? Find a good tutor and good luck!

To put it bluntly, he is still trying to figure out how to teach the class and ways to present the material and tests. If this was any other class, that shouldn't be that big of a problem but since this is a difficult class already, the confusion is not an option since students will come out losing.

I don't think Maness is as bad as people say. Economic theory is supposed to be a tough class and is a gateway to future upper level economics classes. There were only three tests but they were not that bad as long as you put in the time to study and take good notes in class. I got a B+ by going to class and studying a couple nights before tests.

This was one of the worst classes I've taken at TAMU. You are given 3 exams and that's your entire grade. The exams are incredibly difficult. Even with going to lecture, going to tutoring, reading the textbook and looking over his powerpoint, I would struggle to get Cs. He is very inconsistent in his grading and it is unfair to students.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Graded by few things--Test heavy

reviews.comment: This class was hell for me. I was studying blind for the first 2 exams. All we had to go on were the PowerPoint slides. By the last exam, he realized everyone was failing so he started giving us more practice problems which kind of helped. I went to 4.0 for this class quite a bit which was also a waste of time.

Lectures are boring and many people stopped going to class by the end. Only 3 grades are 3 exams (no cumulative final) and are essay style exams done in a blue book. Tests covered chapters, sometimes 100+ pages of reading, and were miserable to study for. If you knew the information well, the questions were not too bad to answer, fair grader

reviews.comment: This professor is extremely lazy and reuses his exam questions every year... the priceless book only has 2 questions or so on the exam but the reading can cover 100+ pages.  And the articles in email are boring and tedious to read with maybe one question from them... easy class , but boring and most skip class because they know how he is.

reviews.comment: Maness is a very smart guy, if you are looking to learn about the healthcare economics this is a perfect class. The exams are 7 short answer but you only have to answer 5. If you pay attention in lecture and understand the material an A is achievable. Make sure you do the assigned readings because there's always a couple questions from them.
